internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Two occurrences call John and Jesus a boy; one has Joseph say he may incline toward the women. A proposal based on youthful inclination imports a participant stereotype rather than extracting a shared root contribution.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: Part of speech and surface form separate the child noun from the inclination verb. Context supplies age in one family and directed attraction in the other.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: The two sabiyyan tokens state age/status without desire, while 12:33 states inclination without youth.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: Youth is defined by inclination; the Quranic occurrences do not assert that generalization.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Any bridge broad enough to cover age and attraction becomes non-distinctive against desire, leaning, and childhood terms.
internal_discovery.rationale: Sparse evidence yields two disconnected families; semantic unity is not forced.
